docs.title: robusta-hmf
docs.text:
jax implementation of robust heteroskedastic matrix factorisation. Robusta like the coffee bean, get it?

Documentation, including the API reference: https://tomhilder.github.io/robusta-hmf

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Easiest is from PyPI either with pip

pip install robusta-hmf

or uv (recommended)

uv add robusta-hmf

Or, you can clone and build from source

git clone git@github.com:TomHilder/robusta-hmf.git
cd robusta-hmf
pip install -e .

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Given a data matrix Y of shape (N, M) and a matching matrix of inverse-variance weights W, fit a rank-K factorisation Y ≈ A @ G.T:

import jax

# JAX defaults to float32, but you should use float64 with robusta
jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

from robusta_hmf import Robusta

# Instantiate a model. Here, of rank 5, with a robust_scale of 2.0
# The rank is the number of basis vectors in the model
# The robust_scale parameter controls how aggressively outliers are downweighted
model = Robusta(rank=5, robust=True, robust_scale=2.0)

# Perform the fit using data matrix Y and weights matrix W
# Both of shape (N, M), and weights should contain inverse variances
state, loss_history = model.fit(Y, W, max_iter=1000)

basis = state.G          # (M, K) shared basis vectors
coeffs = state.A         # (N, K) per-row coefficients

# The model's (robust) prediction of Y
reconstruction = model.synthesize()   # A @ G.T, shape (N, M)

Please refer to the additional documentation below to understand our implementation further. For reference regarding the method itself, see Hilder+2026.

docs.title: Missing data, coverage and regularisation
docs.text:
One should handle missing or masked data entry Y_ij by setting the corresponding entry W_ij to 0. .fit() will ignore any of these values.

Any NaN or inf values in Y or W will be handled automatically by setting them to zero, i.e.: Y_ij = W_ij = 0. In this case, a DataWarning is issued that informs you of how many of these cases there were. Passing Robusta(..., nan_error=True) will escalate this warning to a raised Error, which may be desirable for large-scale or pipeline uses of robusta-hmf.

The coverage of a row or column is its number of non-zero weights. A row of A (one row of Y) or of G (one column of Y) has rank unknowns, so it is determined by the data only if its coverage is at least rank. Rows and columns with less are automatically excluded:

  • Excluded rows and columns do not inform the fit. Their rows of A and G will be set to NaN in the returned fit, to signpost their exclusion. state.row_excluded / state.col_excluded also indicate exclusions, such that .synthesize() and .residuals() will give NaN where the model is undefined. .robust_weights() instead treats excluded entries like missing ones (weight 1), so per-row outlier scores stay finite.
  • When exclusion occurs, an UnderdeterminedWarning will list them. model.fit_info.exclusions also records instances of exclusion as well as why.
  • The returned state can be saved, passed back to fit(init_state=...), or used for infer() and score(). Exclusion will cause the following behaviour for these:
  • fit(init_state=...) recomputes exclusions from the data it is given, so rows and columns that are now covered come back.
  • infer() keeps the columns excluded in training and excludes new rows with too little coverage.
  • score() treats excluded entries as zero-weight and reports how many there were (n_excluded_rows, n_excluded_cols, n_excluded_entries).

If you want to prevent exclusion from occurring (i.e. keep all rows and columns in all cases), you can keep the model defined with regularisation by setting als_ridge. The undetermined entries of A and G are then shrunk towards zero. The larger the ridge is, the more this also impacts other entries of A and G. An UnderdeterminedWarning will tell you which parts of the model are determined only by the ridge and not the data. If the ridge is too small to register at the level of precision, a warning will give the minimum usable value. For example, if you are working with float32 (firstly, probably don't), the ridge will need to be larger than that at float64. With a ridge, the loss being minimised includes the ridge penalty, so the rising-loss check described below is not applied.

As a final note for the nerds, you can easily mix this behaviour by setting entries of Y to zero and the corresponding entries of W to small numbers where you want regularisation. W can then be zero where you want exclusion. In this case, don't use als_ridge.

docs.title: Convergence and warnings
docs.text:
robusta-hmf may issue any of the following warnings:

Warning Means DataWarning NaN or inf input entries were treated as missing. UnderdeterminedWarning Some rows or columns have fewer non-zero weights than rank. ConvergenceWarning The fit stopped at max_iter without converging, or the loss function started increasing.

model.fit_info records how the last fit() went: converged, stop_reason, n_iter, final_loss, loss_rises and exclusions. infer() stores nothing on the model, since one model is often applied to many datasets; its warnings name the number of rows instead.

If you wish for these warnings to instead raise Errors, you can do that simply as follows:

import warnings
from robusta_hmf import ConvergenceWarning
warnings.simplefilter("error", ConvergenceWarning)

docs.title: If the loss rises or diverges
docs.text:
RHMF is an iterative algorithm, and each step involves solving linear systems. In exact arithmetic the loss always decreases. Unfortunately, reality is harsher and matrix solves in floating point arithmetic suffer from round-off.

When the loss rises by more than the expected jitter caused by round-off, it indicates that the matrix solve in one of the iteration steps has lost accuracy (often because of a growing condition number), and a ConvergenceWarning is issued.

Some possible causes of convergence issues are:

  1. float32. Try the fit in float64. If that behaves, the float32 fit was running out of precision in badly conditioned solves.
  2. Regularisation too small. If you set als_ridge, check for the warning above, and either raise the ridge or remove it so under-covered rows and columns are excluded. Note that if you are manually regularising by using tiny weights, robusta will not perform any check for you that the values are large enough for the working precision.
  3. The rank is too large. Rows or columns with coverage only just above rank are determined, but poorly. Try a lower rank.
  4. Your dataset is crazy. In some cases, the initial guess provided by robusta will be very bad, causing very badly conditioned matrix solves. This is problem specific, and so you may have to explore other initialisation strategies.

If the loss becomes NaN or infinite, the fit stops with a FloatingPointError that will state the likely cause.

docs.title: Precision
docs.text:
You should use float64 by default. JAX only provides float64 once jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) has been called, before any JAX array is created. Without it, fit(), infer() and score() raise PrecisionError instead of silently computing in float32.

float32 is supported as an explicit choice, Robusta(..., dtype="float32"), and is much faster on GPUs. It is also less forgiving of badly conditioned solves as explained above.

docs.title: Model selection / cross validation
docs.text:
score() returns the statistics used in the paper. There, we recommended using the KL divergence of the standardised residuals from a standard Normal distribution N(0, 1). For this score, lower is better, and so you should choose a rank (K in the paper) and robust_scale (Q in the paper) that performs well in terms of this score. score() also provides some other potentially useful diagnostics although we do not recommend using them for model selection. Excluded entries count as zero residuals in these scores, so compare scores across ranks only when n_excluded_entries is 0 (or the same) for each.

infer_state, _ = model.infer(Y_test, W_test, state=state)
scores = model.score(Y_test, W_test, state=infer_state)

scores.kl        # KL divergence from N(0, 1); the model-selection criterion
scores.std_z     # sigma_z, target 1
scores.chi2_red  # reduced chi-squared, target 1

In practice, you may get quite good performance just picking the rank from some heuristic arguments (how much diversity do you expect?), and a robust_scale between approx. 2 and 5.

docs.title: Fitting data larger than one GPU
docs.text:
Each iteration in the optimisation over the whole (N, M) data materialises about five full-size intermediates on top of Y and W. As an example, for a problem of size approx. 500,000 x 2500 in float64, this will be about 50 GB of memory. This can be (naively) too much for a single GPU.

Chunking allows you to still run on one GPU. On top of this, one can shard across GPUs to increase the speed of the solve. Both of these are implemented via ShardedFrame:

from robusta_hmf import Robusta, ShardedFrame

model = Robusta(
    rank=10,
    robust_scale=5.0,
    override_frame=ShardedFrame(row_block=4096),  # devices default to all visible
)
state, loss_history = model.fit(Y, W)

Everything else (infer, synthesize, score, coefficients, residuals) works the same as usual. Y and W are stored on device in float32 by default while all arithmetic happens in the model's dtype (float64 unless you opt in to float32), halving local memory used by Y and W.

To fit several models to one sample (say a (K, Q) grid) without re-transferring the data, use the following pattern:

frame = ShardedFrame(row_block=4096)
data, _ = frame.prepare(Y, W)          # one transfer to device
for rank in ranks:
    model = Robusta(rank=rank, override_frame=frame)
    state, _ = model.fit(data)

The data are checked for NaN and inf when prepare() places them, so pass frame.prepare(Y, W, nan_error=True) there if you want an error rather than a warning.

docs.title: Customisation
docs.text: Hooks for changing how a fit is initialised, when it stops, and how its loop is scheduled. Pass them to Robusta as override_initialiser, override_conv_tester and override_frame.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.Initialiser dataclass
docs.text:
Seeds (A, G) before the optimisation loop starts.

Pass one to Robusta as override_initialiser. N, M and K may be left unset, in which case Robusta.fit() fills them in from the data, so an initialiser can be built without knowing the shapes up front.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default N int | None

Rows and columns of Y, and the rank.

None M int | None

Rows and columns of Y, and the rank.

None K int | None

Rows and columns of Y, and the rank.

None strategy (svd, random, custom)

"svd": A = U S^½ and G = V S^½ from the leading K singular values and vectors of Y (the zero-filled data, without the weights). "random": independent standard normals. "custom": the A and G passed to execute().

"svd"

docs.title: robusta_hmf.ConvergenceTester dataclass
docs.text:
Decides when a fit has converged, from consecutive checked states.

Robusta builds one from conv_strategy and conv_tol; pass one as override_conv_tester to set it directly.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default strategy (max_frac_G, max_frac_A, rel_frac_loss, none)

"max_frac_G": converged when max((G_new - G_old)²) / mean(G_new²) is below tol, i.e. the largest change in any entry of G is small compared with the typical size of G. "max_frac_A": the same for A (used by infer(), where G is fixed). "rel_frac_loss": converged when |loss_new - loss_old| / |loss_new| is below tol. "none": never converged, so the fit runs to max_iter.

"max_frac_G" tol float

Tolerance. Note that Robusta passes its own conv_tol (default 1e-3).

1e-6

docs.title: robusta_hmf.OptFrame dataclass
docs.text:
Owns the optimisation loop: data placement, initialisation, iteration.

Robusta configures the model (an HMF) and delegates execution to a frame. A subclass can change how the loop is scheduled -- see ShardedFrame, which chunks and shards the row axis -- without re-declaring the model's parameter list.

compute_dtype is the dtype of the arithmetic and of A/G. Robusta sets it through bind(); None leaves arrays in whatever dtype they arrive in.

docs.title: Diagnostics, warnings and errors
docs.text: model.fit_info records how the last fit() ran. Warnings all derive from RobustaWarning, so warnings.simplefilter("error", RobustaWarning) turns every one of them into an error.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.FitInfo dataclass
docs.text:
How a call to Robusta.fit() ran.

Attributes:

Name Type Description converged bool

Whether the convergence test passed.

stop_reason {converged, max_iter}

Why the loop ended.

n_iter int

Number of iterations run.

final_loss float

Loss at the last iteration (NaN if no iteration ran).

loss_rises tuple of int

Iterations at which the loss rose by more than the optimiser allows.

exclusions tuple of ExclusionEvent

Every exclusion, in the order it happened.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.ExclusionEvent dataclass
docs.text:
Rows or columns removed from a fit because the data could not determine them.

Exclusion happens before the first iteration, from the weights.

Attributes:

Name Type Description axis {row, col}

Whether indices are rows (of Y and A) or columns (of Y, rows of G).

indices tuple of int

The excluded indices, sorted.

cause {empty, low_coverage, cascade}

"empty": no non-zero weights. "low_coverage": fewer non-zero weights than the rank. "cascade": fell below the rank after other rows or columns were excluded.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.RobustaWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Base class for warnings issued by robusta-hmf.

Filter on it to act on all of them at once, e.g. warnings.simplefilter("error", RobustaWarning) turns every robusta-hmf warning into an exception.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.DataWarning
docs.text:
Bases: RobustaWarning

The input data were modified before use.

Issued by fit(), infer() and score() (or prepare() on a frame) when entries of Y or W are NaN or infinite: those entries are treated as missing (Y = W = 0), and the message says how many there were. Pass nan_error=True to raise ValueError instead.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.UnderdeterminedWarning
docs.text:
Bases: RobustaWarning

Some rows or columns have fewer usable weights than the rank.

Their factors are not determined by the data: a row of A (or of G) has rank unknowns and needs at least that many non-zero weights. Without als_ridge these rows and columns are excluded from the fit and returned as NaN (see FitInfo.exclusions); with als_ridge they are kept, determined only by the ridge, and the warning names them.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.ConvergenceWarning
docs.text:
Bases: RobustaWarning

The fit did not converge, or its loss rose when it should not.

Issued when a fit or inference reaches max_iter before the convergence test passes, and (for ALS without a ridge) when the loss rises by more than floating-point round-off allows, which in exact arithmetic it never does. A rise usually means a badly conditioned least-squares solve: try float64, a smaller rank, or check W.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.PrecisionError
docs.text:
Bases: RuntimeError

A fit asked for float64 but JAX's float64 support is disabled.

JAX computes in float32 unless jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) is called before any JAX array is created. Rather than silently running a float64 model in float32, fit(), infer() and score() raise this. Enable x64, or pass dtype="float32" to Robusta to choose float32 explicitly.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Held-out scores for model selection. Robusta.score() returns a ZMoments; read .kl for the paper's cross-validation score. The functions below compute the same quantities directly from arrays.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.ZMoments dataclass
docs.text:
Sufficient statistics for the moment-based held-out scores.

Attributes:

Name Type Description n int

Number of residuals summed over, N * M. Every pixel counts, including those masked to zero weight, matching the convention used throughout the paper's analysis scripts.

sum_z, sum_z2 float

sum(z) and sum(z**2).

sum_chi2 float

sum(W * r**2), the unrobustified chi-squared.

n_excluded_rows, n_excluded_cols int

Rows and columns the scored state excludes (see RHMFState). Their entries enter the sums as zero-weight entries do: z and chi-squared are 0 there, but they still count in n.

n_excluded_entries int

Entries with non-zero weight that fall in an excluded row or column.

docs.title: mean_z property
docs.text: Mean of the robustly-weighted residuals. Target: 0.

docs.title: var_z property
docs.text: Variance of the robustly-weighted residuals. Target: 1.

docs.title: std_z property
docs.text: Standard deviation of the robustly-weighted residuals. Target: 1.

docs.title: chi2_red property
docs.text: Reduced chi-squared, mean(W * r**2). Target: 1.

docs.title: rmse property
docs.text: Weighted RMSE, sqrt(chi2_red). Lower is better.

docs.title: kl property
docs.text:
KL divergence of the z distribution from N(0, 1). Target: 0.

The paper's model-selection score (Eq. 20). See kl_from_moments(). Lower is better.

docs.title: as_dict()
docs.text: The scores as a plain dict, for tabulating over a (K, Q) grid.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.kl_from_moments(mean_z, std_z)
docs.text:
KL divergence from N(mean_z, std_z^2) to N(0, 1). Target: 0.

The paper's model-selection score (Eq. 20), under a Gaussian approximation to the empirical distribution of the standardised residuals:

.. math:: \mathrm{KL} = -\log\sigma_z + (\sigma_z^2 + \mu_z^2) / 2 - 1/2

which is zero only for :math:\mu_z = 0, \sigma_z = 1 and positive otherwise. Lower is better.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.z_scores(Y, W, A, G, likelihood)
docs.text:
Robustly-weighted standardised residuals.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default Y (Array, shape(N, M))

Data matrix.

required W (Array, shape(N, M))

Data weights (inverse variance).

required A (Array, shape(N, K))

Coefficients.

Supplies the IRLS downweighting.

required

z = (Y - A @ G.T) * sqrt(W * w_irls), which is unit normal under a calibrated model whose outliers are correctly downweighted.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.mad_z(Y, W, A, G, likelihood)

Not available from ZMoments: a median needs the whole (N, M) z array, so this has no out-of-core equivalent.

docs.title: Robusta
docs.text: The model class, the state it returns, and saving and loading that state. These are all importable from the top-level robusta_hmf namespace, except RHMFState, which lives in robusta_hmf.state and is what fit() and infer() return.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.Robusta dataclass
docs.text:
Robust heteroskedastic matrix factorisation (RHMF) of a data matrix.

Factorises an (N, M) data matrix Y with inverse-variance weights W as Y ≈ A @ G.T, where A (N, K) holds per-row coefficients and G (M, K) holds K shared basis vectors (K is rank). Missing entries are entries with W = 0.

With robust=True (the default) the fit maximises a Student-t likelihood by iteratively reweighted least squares: each iteration computes per-entry robust weights Q² / (Q² + W r²), where r is the residual and Q² = robust_nu · robust_scale², then solves weighted least squares for A and then G, then rotates so the columns of G are orthonormal. Entries the model cannot explain get robust weights near 0, which flags them as outliers. With robust=False it is plain heteroskedastic matrix factorisation (HMF).

The interface follows scikit-learn: fit() learns A and G, infer() finds coefficients for new rows with G held fixed, score() scores held-out data for choosing rank and robust_scale, and robust_weights() returns the per-entry outlier weights. The model keeps the state of its last fit(), which the other methods use when no state is passed.

Examples:

>>> import jax
>>> jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
>>> from robusta_hmf import Robusta
>>> model = Robusta(rank=5, robust_scale=3.0)
>>> state, loss_history = model.fit(Y, W)
>>> weights = model.robust_weights(Y, W)        # (N, M), 1 = inlier
>>> per_row = jnp.quantile(weights, 0.01, axis=1)  # one outlier score per row

docs.title: A property
docs.text: A (N, K) from the last fit(), or None before fitting.

docs.title: G property
docs.text: G (M, K) from the last fit(), or None before fitting.

docs.title: state property
docs.text:
The RHMFState of the last fit().

None before fitting.

docs.title: loss_history property
docs.text: The loss after each iteration of the last fit(), or None before fitting.

docs.title: fit_info property
docs.text:
The FitInfo of the last fit(), or None before fitting.

Not updated by infer().

docs.title: __init__(rank, method='als', robust=True, robust_nu=1.0, robust_scale=1.0, init_strategy='svd', override_initialiser=None, conv_strategy='max_frac_G', conv_tol=0.001, override_conv_tester=None, override_frame=None, als_ridge=None, learning_rate=0.001, rotation='fast', dtype=None, nan_error=False, **rotation_kwargs)
docs.text:
Configure a model. Nothing is computed until fit().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rank int

Number of basis vectors, K. It must be chosen before fitting (unlike PCA, the components of a rank-K fit are not the first K of a larger fit); score() on held-out data helps choose it.

required method (als, sgd)

"als": iteratively reweighted alternating least squares, the algorithm of the paper. "sgd": gradient descent on the loss with optax (Adafactor unless overridden).

"als" robust bool

If True, use the Student-t likelihood, which downweights outliers; if False, use a Gaussian likelihood (plain HMF, all robust weights 1).

True robust_nu float

Student-t degrees of freedom. The fit depends on robust_nu and robust_scale only through Q² = robust_nu · robust_scale², so the default of 1 (a Cauchy likelihood) loses nothing.

1.0 robust_scale float

The soft outlier threshold Q (with robust_nu=1), in units of the measurement uncertainty: residuals much smaller than Q / sqrt(W) are treated as Gaussian noise, much larger ones are downweighted. Values of roughly 2 to 5 are typical starting points.

1.0 init_strategy (svd, random)

How A and G are seeded. "svd" uses the leading rank singular vectors of Y (scaled by the square roots of the singular values); "random" draws standard normals from seed. To start from factors you already have, pass init_state to fit() instead.

"svd" override_initialiser Initialiser | None

Custom initialiser; replaces init_strategy if given.

None conv_strategy str

Convergence test, checked every conv_check_cadence iterations: "max_frac_G" (largest squared change in G relative to the mean square of G), "max_frac_A" (the same for A), "rel_frac_loss" (relative change in the loss) or "none" (run to max_iter).

"max_frac_G" conv_tol float

Tolerance for conv_strategy.

1e-3 override_conv_tester ConvergenceTester | None

Custom convergence tester; replaces conv_strategy and conv_tol if given.

None override_frame OptFrame | None

Custom optimisation frame, which owns how the loop is scheduled. Defaults to a plain OptFrame that evaluates each step over the whole matrix. Pass ShardedFrame to chunk and shard the row axis, for data larger than one device's memory.

None als_ridge float | None

Ridge added to the diagonal of every least-squares solve for A and G (method="als" only). Without it, rows and columns with fewer non-zero weights than rank are excluded from the fit; with it they are kept and shrunk towards zero, and an UnderdeterminedWarning names them.

None learning_rate float

Learning rate of the default Adafactor optimiser (method="sgd" only).

1e-3 rotation (fast, slow, identity)

How A and G are rotated after each update to remove the factorisation's K × K degeneracy, leaving A @ G.T unchanged. "fast" makes the columns of G orthonormal by symmetric whitening (K × K eigendecomposition). "slow" uses an SVD so that G is orthonormal and the columns of A are orthogonal and ordered by decreasing norm, like PCA. "identity" does not rotate.

"fast" dtype (float64, float32)

Precision of the fit. Y, W, A and G are cast to it. float64 needs JAX's float64 support, enabled with jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) before any JAX array is created; without it, fitting raises PrecisionError rather than silently running in float32. float32 is faster, especially on GPUs, but can diverge when rows or columns of W have fewer non-zero weights than rank, so it has to be requested explicitly. When None, a compute_dtype set on override_frame is used, else float64.

"float64" nan_error bool

What fit(), infer() and score() do with entries where Y or W is NaN or infinite. With False they are treated as missing (Y = W = 0 there) and one DataWarning is issued; with True they raise ValueError. Negative weights always raise.

False **rotation_kwargs

Passed to the rotation. For "fast": target ("G", the default, or "A": which factor is made orthonormal), whiten (default True) and eps (default 1e-6, floor on the eigenvalues).

{}

docs.title: set_state(state)
docs.text:
Return a copy of this model holding state as its fitted state.

Use it to restore a saved fit without refitting, e.g. with a state from load_state_from_npz(), so that methods called without state use it. The model itself is left unchanged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default state RHMFState

The state the copy should hold.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description model Robusta

A deep copy of this model with state set. Its loss_history and fit_info are those of this model.

docs.title: fit(Y, W=None, max_iter=1000, rotation_cadence=1, conv_check_cadence=10, seed=0, init_state=None)
docs.text:
Fit A and G to data, and keep the result on the model.

Iterates until the convergence test passes or max_iter is reached, printing the loss at every convergence check. Rows and columns of W with fewer non-zero weights than rank are excluded first (unless als_ridge is set), since the data cannot determine their factors; see FitInfo for how the run is recorded.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default Y (Array, shape(N, M))

Data matrix. May instead be a handle returned by the frame's prepare() (e.g. a ShardedData), in which case W is carried inside it and the W argument is ignored. Reuse that handle to fit several models to one sample without re-transferring it.

required W (Array, shape(N, M))

Inverse-variance weights, 1 / σ². Required unless Y is a prepared handle. Zero marks a missing entry. Entries where Y or W is NaN or infinite are treated as missing (or raise, with nan_error=True); negative weights raise ValueError.

None max_iter int

Maximum number of iterations.

1000 rotation_cadence int

Rotate every this many iterations. ALS always rotates every iteration (another value only triggers a warning); this matters for method="sgd".

1 conv_check_cadence int

Test convergence (and print the loss) every this many iterations.

10 seed int

Random seed, used by init_strategy="random".

0 init_state RHMFState | None

Start from this state instead of initialising, e.g. to continue a fit or to start from factors computed elsewhere. Its A and G must have shapes (N, rank) and (M, rank). Exclusions are recomputed from W, so rows and columns the state excluded come back if W now covers them.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description state RHMFState

The fitted factors. Excluded rows of A and G are NaN and marked by state.row_excluded / state.col_excluded.

loss_history (Array, shape(n_iter))

The loss after each iteration.

Raises:

Type Description PrecisionError

If the model's dtype is float64 and JAX's float64 support is off.

FloatingPointError

If the loss or the factors become NaN or infinite.

Warns:

Type Description UnderdeterminedWarning

If rows or columns are excluded (or, with als_ridge, are determined only by the ridge).

ConvergenceWarning

If the fit reaches max_iter without converging, or the loss rises by more than round-off allows.

DataWarning

If NaN or infinite entries were treated as missing.

Notes

After the fit, fit_info records whether it converged, the number of iterations, any loss rises and any exclusions.

docs.title: synthesize(state=None, indices=None)
docs.text:
The model's reconstruction of the data, A @ G.T.

Because outliers are downweighted in the fit, this is the low-rank description of each row without its outliers; Y minus this is where they show up (see residuals()).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default state RHMFState | None

State to use, e.g. the output of infer(). If None, use the last fit.

None indices Array | None

If given, reconstruct only these rows (indices into A).

None

Returns:

Name Type Description synthesis (Array, shape(N, M) or (len(indices), M))

The reconstruction. NaN in rows and columns the state excludes, where the model is undefined.

docs.title: infer(Y_infer, W_infer=None, state=None, max_iter=100, conv_strategy='max_frac_A', conv_tol=0.001, conv_check_cadence=10)
docs.text:
Infer coefficients for new rows with the basis G held fixed.

Alternates the robust-weight update and the least-squares solve for A (never G), starting from a weighted least-squares fit with the data weights alone. Always uses least squares, even for a model fitted with method="sgd". Runs through the same frame as fit(), so a sharded model infers on sharded data with the same chunking. The model's stored state is not changed, since one model is often applied to many datasets.

Use it to apply a trained basis to held-out data before score(), or to new data; then call robust_weights() with the returned state to find outliers in the new rows.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default Y_infer Array, shape (N', M)

New data with the same M columns as the training data, or a handle from the frame's prepare().

required W_infer Array, shape (N', M)

Inverse-variance weights for Y_infer. Required unless Y_infer is a prepared handle.

None state RHMFState | None

State supplying the fixed basis. If None, use the last fit. Columns it excludes stay excluded; new rows with fewer than rank non-zero weights in the other columns are excluded.

None max_iter int

Maximum iterations.

100 conv_strategy str

Convergence strategy. "max_frac_G" is meaningless here (G is fixed) and is switched to "max_frac_A" with a warning.

"max_frac_A" conv_tol float

Convergence tolerance.

1e-3 conv_check_cadence int

How often to check convergence.

10

Returns:

Name Type Description state RHMFState

A of shape (N', rank) for the new rows (NaN for excluded rows), with G unchanged.

loss_history (Array, shape(n_iter))

The loss after each iteration.

docs.title: score(Y, W=None, state=None)
docs.text:
Held-out scores for a state, as sufficient statistics.

Computes the standardised residuals z = (Y - A @ G.T) · sqrt(W · w_robust), which follow N(0, 1) when the model is calibrated and the outliers are correctly downweighted, and summarises them. .kl, the KL divergence of a Gaussian with the mean and standard deviation of z from N(0, 1), is the model-selection score of the paper: lower is better. Read it alongside a goodness-of-fit measure such as .chi2_red, since a rank that is too small with an aggressive robust_scale can also score well by downweighting most of the data.

Typical use is cross-validation over rank and robust_scale: fit() on a training split, infer() on the held-out split, then score the inferred state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default Y (Array, shape(N, M))

Held-out data, or a handle from the frame's prepare().

required W (Array, shape(N, M))

Held-out weights.

None state RHMFState | None

State to score, normally the output of infer(). If None, use the last fit.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description moments ZMoments

Read .kl for the paper's model-selection score (Eq. 20), or .std_z, .chi2_red, .rmse. Accumulated chunk by chunk when the frame is sharded, so this never forms an (N, M) array.

See Also

robusta_hmf.metrics.mad_z : needs the full residual array, so it is not available here.

docs.title: robust_weights(Y, W, state=None)
docs.text:
Per-entry robust weights, the outlier measure of RHMF.

w = Q² / (Q² + W r²) with r = Y - A @ G.T and Q² = robust_nu · robust_scale²: 1 for an entry the model fits exactly, falling towards 0 as the residual grows past about Q standard deviations. Summarise them per row for an outlier score per object, e.g. the median or a low quantile (the paper uses the 1% quantile and flags rows below 0.5), or per column for one per feature. With robust=False every weight is 1.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default Y (Array, shape(N, M))

The data the state describes.

required W (Array, shape(N, M))

Inverse-variance weights for Y. Entries with W = 0 get weight 1.

required state RHMFState | None

State to use, e.g. the output of infer() for new data. If None, use the last fit.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description weights (Array, shape(N, M))

Robust weights in (0, 1]. Entries in rows or columns the state excludes are treated like missing data and get weight 1, so per-row summaries stay finite; state.row_excluded / col_excluded mark them.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.state.RHMFState
docs.text:
Bases: Module

The factors A and G of Y ≈ A Gᵀ, plus loop bookkeeping.

Returned by Robusta.fit() and Robusta.infer(), and accepted by the other methods of Robusta as state. An Equinox module, so it is an immutable JAX pytree. Save and load it with save_state_to_npz() and load_state_from_npz().

Attributes:

Name Type Description A (Array, shape(N, K))

Coefficients, one row per row of Y.

G (Array, shape(M, K))

Basis vectors, one column per component and one row per column of Y.

it int

Number of iterations run to reach this state.

opt_state OptState | None

Optimiser state for method="sgd"; None for ALS.

row_excluded Array of bool, shape (N,), or None

Rows of Y the fit excluded because the data did not determine them (fewer non-zero weights than the rank). Their rows of A are NaN. None means no row is excluded.

col_excluded Array of bool, shape (M,), or None

The same for columns of Y, whose rows of G are NaN.

docs.title: Sharded fitting
docs.text: Row-chunked, multi-device fitting for data larger than one GPU. Pass a ShardedFrame to Robusta(override_frame=...); everything else works as for a dense fit.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.ShardedFrame dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: OptFrame

An OptFrame that chunks and shards the rows.

Reads the likelihood, rotation and ALS ridge off the HMF it is bound to, so it never duplicates the model's parameter list. Hand it to Robusta via override_frame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default row_block int

Target rows per scan chunk. Sets peak scratch memory, roughly 6 * row_block * M * itemsize bytes per device -- ~440 MiB at M=2321, K=10, float64. Larger is marginally faster, smaller is safer.

4096 devices Sequence | None

Devices to shard over. Defaults to all visible devices; a single device gives pure chunking, which is the memory fix on its own.

None store_dtype dtype

On-device dtype for Y and W. Measurements are usually float32 to begin with, and all arithmetic still happens in compute_dtype.

numpy.float32 compute_dtype dtype | None

Dtype of the arithmetic and of A/G. When None, it comes from the dtype of the Robusta model the frame is bound to (float64 by default). Setting it here is the same explicit choice as passing dtype to Robusta; setting both to different values is an error.

None verbose bool

Print the sharding and memory summary when the data is placed.

True Notes

Results are not bitwise identical to Robusta's dense path, nor across different row_block or device counts: the arithmetic is the same but the summation order is not. See the module docstring.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.RowPlan dataclass
docs.text:
How n_rows real rows are laid out over devices and scan chunks.

shard_map needs every device to hold the same number of rows, and the inner lax.scan needs that number to be an exact multiple of the chunk size, so the row axis is padded up to n_padded. The chunk size is shrunk from the requested row_block where that makes the padding smaller -- for the full RVS sample on 4 devices this is 18 padded rows rather than the 8082 a fixed 8192-row block would need.

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_rows int

Real rows, before padding.

n_devices int

Devices in the mesh.

chunk int

Rows per lax.scan step. Sets peak scratch memory.

n_chunks int

Scan steps per device.

docs.title: robusta_hmf.GramInitialiser dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: Initialiser

SVD initialisation via the Gram matrix, for data too large to svd.

Identical in exact arithmetic to svd_init(): for Y = U S V.T, Y.T @ Y = V S^2 V.T, so the top-K eigenvectors of the Gram matrix are V[:, :K] and Y @ V = U S. This returns A = U sqrt(S) and G = V sqrt(S), matching the library's convention, without ever forming the (N, min(N, M)) U that jnp.linalg.svd wants -- which for the Gaia RVS sample is as large as Y itself.

Equivalent does not mean identical in floating point: forming Y.T @ Y squares the condition number, so the recovered subspace agrees with svd_init at around sqrt(eps) (~1e-8 in float64) rather than eps. This is an initialiser, and the first few ALS iterations wash the difference out -- fits started from either route agree to ~1e-12 -- but do not expect bitwise agreement at iteration zero.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default N int | None

Filled in by Robusta.fit() when left unset.

None M int | None

Filled in by Robusta.fit() when left unset.

None K int | None

Filled in by Robusta.fit() when left unset.

None strategy (svd, random, custom)

"svd" takes the Gram route; the others behave as usual but place their output on the mesh.

"svd" frame ShardedFrame | None

The frame supplying the mesh and row plan. Filled in automatically when Robusta builds the initialiser.

None
